case_traceability: Each checklist item must remain traceable to one or more Table IX cases (bidirectional checklist-case link).
sync_note: Item text is meaning-aligned with manuscript Table XI (v1.0.19). Items 3a–3e split the former monolithic item 3; item 10 is the expanded dual-IdP semantic-equivalence template.

items.item: Treat IdP success and edge release as separate steps; require acknowledgment before commit, or compensating rollback.
Do not key device caps on randomized MACs; use stable bindings and remediation user experience.
Define the edge callback capability and its trust boundary (distinct from OAuth state, authorization code, access token, and OIDC nonce).

Implement a single-winner, one-time consume operation at the consistency scope of the edge release action; a linearizable primitive is one sufficient implementation when concurrent readers and writers share that scope.
Document replication, failover, partition, and uncertain-outcome behavior; fail closed when the consume result cannot be determined.
Size the callback-value TTL from measured high-percentile authorization round-trip behavior plus a bounded operational margin.
Test concurrent legitimate callbacks and repeated presentation of the same capability.
Document two session planes; never skip edge re-authorization because SSO is warm.

Derive directory-federation timeouts from measured worst-site WAN behavior and configured LDAP/AD retry behavior; do not reuse latency assumptions from unrelated HA or database-replication paths; plan degrade messaging.
Validate sticky routing and shared session stores across sites; expect re-authentication windows on failover.
Treat IdP cluster coherence as an authentication health check; quorum runbooks; no dual-writer under partition.

Validate representative end-to-end SAML and OIDC request sizes against the deployed gateway version and configuration, including request limits, buffering behaviour, and timeouts; alert on gateway rejection, malformed federation payloads, and timeout termination.
items.note: No buffer default is prescribed. harness/fixtures/i4/ provides synthetic size-class fixtures for local validation only.

items.item: Provide at least one alternative authenticator that does not depend on SMS/PSTN delivery; do not make SMS the sole MFA completion path for affected users.

Before dual-IdP cutover or migration, complete a minimal semantic-equivalence checklist: issuer (iss) and subject (sub) stability; audience (aud) and authorized-party bindings; claim names and value encodings; group/role representation; access- and ID-token lifetimes and clock skew tolerance; signing-key / JWKS rotation and key-id handling; logout and session-end semantics. Treat shared directory membership as necessary but not sufficient.
